summary: Six state consumer advocates jointly protest PJM's Reliability Backstop Procurement in ER26-3380, ask FERC to reject it as unjust and unreasonable, offer two alternatives, and list conditions if FERC accepts it.
ask: Reject the RBP; direct PJM to refile a subscription-based procurement or advance the effective date of its IRAS proposal; if RBP is accepted, impose conditions such as a five-year procurement period.

points.point: The advocates say RBP cost allocation to large loads depends on state action, and where states do not act, zonal charges fall on the general ratepayer body.
points.quote: where a state does not act—or acts late—zonal RBP charges are allocated onto the general ratepayer body within the

points.point: They say RBP's design contradicts its stated 6.8 GW reliability need through opt-outs, 15-year terms and no market mitigation.
points.quote: PJM says that reliability demands that nearly 7 gigawatts of new supply be procured in the near-term, yet permits an untold number of megawatts (or possibly gigawatts) to opt-out of the auction

points.point: They say the $555/MW-day price ceiling comes from a one-year capacity design and does not fit a commitment of up to 15 years.
points.quote: A cap set on that basis is irrelevant to the determination of what should be paid

points.point: They put 15 years of RBP charges on a 6,831 MW total at about $20.8 billion.
points.quote: $555/MW-day x 365 days x 15 years would be $20,756,847,375.

points.point: Option One: refile as a subscription model in which load-serving entities set the procurement quantity and bear credit obligations.
points.quote: PJM should be directed to refile the RBP as a "subscription" model

points.point: Option Two: advance IRAS so large loads from 2028/2029 either bring their own resources or are treated as first-off in emergencies.
points.quote: the Commission should, in lieu of approving the RBP, advance the effective date of IRAS

points.point: As a fallback, they ask that any approval limit the procurement period to five years.
points.quote: The Commission should limit the RBP procurement period to five years

throughLine.text: Protest in PJM's separate backstop procurement docket ER26-3380, which the advocates link to the EL26-67 show cause order they say already found PJM's tariff appears unjust and unreasonable.
